audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells you to 'trade strictly around Drunken Rage' and treats it as a tracked cooldown. Drunken Rage is a flat 5 seconds — it is effectively always available, so there is no cooldown window to trade into.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Gragas samples his latest brew for 1 second. After finishing, he becomes boisterous and belligerent, dealing magic damage to all nearby enemies on his next basic attack and reducing damage received.' Cooldown 5 at every rank. The real tell is the one-second drink animation before the buff exists, not a cooldown timer. Coaching a player to wait for a 5-second cooldown means waiting forever; coaching them to punish the drink is actionable.
audit.corrected: Drunken Rage is flat 5s and always up — the window is the 1-second drink before the damage reduction applies, not a cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice on this matchup, and every spike is written without a number: Body Slam, Barrel Roll and Explosive Cask are all named with no timings.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 at 600 range — it barely scales, so a single number covers the whole lane. Barrel Roll is 10 down to 6s at 850. Explosive Cask is 100/85/70 at 1000. Those three numbers turn every 'respect it' on the page into something a player can count.
audit.corrected: Body Slam 14s at rank 1 and only 12s at rank 5, 600 range. Barrel Roll 10 to 6s. Explosive Cask 100 to 70s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most useful interaction in the lane is absent: Barrel Roll's explosion grows stronger the longer the cask sits, up to 4 seconds.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Gragas rolls his cask to a location, which can be activated to explode or will explode on its own after 4 seconds. The potency of the explosion increases over time.' That means walking through a freshly-thrown cask costs a fraction of what a ripened one costs, and it means the moment he throws the cask you should either step through it immediately or leave the radius entirely — hovering at the edge for two seconds is the worst option and it is exactly what a player does by default.
audit.corrected: Barrel Roll ripens for up to 4 seconds and hits harder the longer it sits. Cross it early or leave the radius — never linger at its edge.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Happy Hour 'passive regeneration' twice and gives no Grievous Wounds timing.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill.' It is cast-triggered, not idle regen. That changes the counterplay completely — he heals himself by throwing casks at the wave, so denying him idle time does nothing and only anti-heal does. _missing-interactions flags needs-antiheal for this exact pairing.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour heals him when he casts, not while he stands still — he tops up off wave clear, so Grievous Wounds is the only answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block reads 'Gragas Body Slam: His engage. E-slow + kite it.' with no numbers and no second entry.
audit.why: Rewritten with Body Slam's 14-to-12s and 600 range, plus Explosive Cask's 100-to-70s, which is the ability the level-6 advice actually hangs on.
audit.corrected: Body Slam 14 to 12s at 600 range; Explosive Cask 100 to 70s.

edits.after: At Level 1 this is genuinely even — Flamespitter pressures him, but Happy Hour heals him whenever he casts, so poke he can answer by throwing a cask at the wave is poke you have wasted. At Level 2 he can Body Slam onto you from 600 and chain a Barrel Roll before you process the engage, and Drunken Rage cuts the damage you were counting on. The tell is the drink: it takes a full second before the reduction exists, so punish during it. By Level 3 Electro Harpoon is the matchup-defining tool — land it BEFORE Body Slam commits, kill the gap-close, and walk him through your cone. Body Slam is 14 seconds at rank 1 and still 12 at rank 5, so once it is spent, the lane is yours for a long count.
edits.before: At Level 1 this is genuinely even — Flamespitter pressures him but Gragas's passive heals back chip damage, so don't burn all your Heat chasing a trade he can just walk away from after healing. At Level 2 he can Body Slam (E) onto you and chain a full Barrel Roll (Q) explosion before you even process the engage, and his Drunken Rage (W) eats a significant chunk of your Flamespitter's value — respect that. By Level 3 your Electro-Harpoon (E) becomes the matchup-defining tool: land it BEFORE he commits his Body Slam so you slow his approach and deny the free gap-close, then walk him through your Flamespitter cone. Never let him set the trade terms with E-first or you're eating a full rotation with no counterplay beyond your shield.

edits.after: Levels 4-5 his trades keep winning: Drunken Rage is a flat 5 seconds, so it is up for every exchange and there is no cooldown window to wait for — only the 1-second drink. Watch his casks instead. Barrel Roll ripens for up to 4 seconds and its explosion grows the whole time, so step through a fresh one or leave the radius, and never sit at its edge deciding. His Level 6 changes the lane differently from yours: Explosive Cask is 100 seconds at rank 1 and can punt you off your Equalizer placement or into his jungle, so plant the wall only after he spends it. Freeze near your tower and make him walk in rather than chasing Body Slam across the lane.
edits.before: Levels 4-5 Gragas's trades keep winning because his W's flat damage reduction scales well against your burst window and his Q sustain keeps him healthier than he should be — you are not going to short-trade him out of lane. His Level 6 is a lane-changer in a different way than yours: Explosive Cask (R) can knock you AWAY from your Equalizer placement zone, interrupt your pattern entirely, or dump you into his jungle for a gank, so do not plant The Equalizer unless he has already used his R or you have him cornered. Play the wave — freeze near your tower, let him walk into Flamespitter range rather than chasing his E across the lane, and use your Scrap Shield aggressively to absorb his Q burst before retaliating.

notes: Three corrections that change how the lane is played. (1) The page told you to trade around Drunken Rage's cooldown; it is flat 5 seconds and always available, so the only real window is the 1-second drink before the damage reduction applies. (2) Happy Hour was described as 'passive regeneration' — Riot's text says he heals periodically upon USING A SKILL, so he refills off wave clear and anti-heal, not patience, is the answer. (3) Barrel Roll's potency increases over its 4-second fuse, which was never stated anywhere and is the difference between crossing a cask for a scratch and eating a full explosion. The _missing-interactions 'autoreset (Drunken Rage W)' claim was not asserted: Riot's text describes bonus magic damage on his next basic attack, which is an empowered attack, not an attack reset. rumble.json's derived 'knockup' and 'terrain' flags on Scrap Shield remain contradicted by its own description and were ignored.
